options.a: Trailer kingpin area squarely
options.b: Trailer landing gear pads first
options.c: Kingpin at an angle, off center
options.d: Kingpin with jaws already closed

distractorExplanations.b: The landing gear supports the trailer on the ground; the fifth wheel meets the trailer at the kingpin and apron.
distractorExplanations.c: Backing under at an angle can damage the landing gear and miss the jaws; back straight under the kingpin.
distractorExplanations.d: The fifth-wheel jaws must be open to accept the kingpin; closed jaws cannot lock around it.

options.a: Properly connected to matching gladhands
options.b: Crossed if the trailer has spring brakes
options.c: Connected service first, supply optional
options.d: Stored on the dummy couplers while towing

distractorExplanations.b: Lines are never crossed; supply goes to supply and service to service, or trailer brakes will not work correctly.
distractorExplanations.c: Both lines are required: the supply line charges the trailer and releases its springs, service applies brakes.
distractorExplanations.d: Dummy couplers are used when bobtailing; with a trailer both lines must be coupled to its gladhands.

options.a: Kingpin is captured—still verify visually/tug
options.b: Trailer is coupled; no visual check is needed
options.c: Jaws are open and ready to accept the kingpin
options.d: Trailer brakes are set and lines are connected

distractorExplanations.b: A locked indicator can be wrong (for example a high hook); the CDL manual requires a visual check and tug test.
distractorExplanations.c: That is the unlocked position before coupling; a locked indication means the jaws have closed.
distractorExplanations.d: The jaw lock indication concerns the kingpin only; air line connection and brakes are checked separately.

options.a: No effect, since both lines carry the same pressure
options.b: Trailer brakes apply incorrectly / unsafe response
options.c: Tractor brakes failing while trailer brakes work normally
options.d: Faster trailer brake release when the knob is pushed

distractorExplanations.a: Supply and service lines do different jobs; crossing them can leave the trailer without brakes or unable to release.
distractorExplanations.c: Crossed lines affect the trailer's brakes, not the tractor's own service brakes.
distractorExplanations.d: Crossed lines send air to the wrong circuit; the trailer brakes may not release or may not apply.

options.a: Weight distribution and off-tracking
options.b: Trailer brake timing and air pressure
options.c: Kingpin height and coupling strength
options.d: Tractor protection valve operation

distractorExplanations.b: Brake timing depends on valves and lines; sliding the fifth wheel changes axle weights and off-tracking.
distractorExplanations.c: Fifth-wheel height is a separate adjustment; sliding moves the coupling point forward or back.
distractorExplanations.d: The tractor protection valve is an air-system component unaffected by fifth-wheel position.

options.a: Disconnect the air lines first, then lower the landing gear fully
options.b: Lower landing gear, secure trailer, disconnect lines carefully
options.c: Unlock the fifth wheel first, then lower the landing gear
options.d: Release trailer brakes, then lower landing gear on the grade

distractorExplanations.a: The trailer is secured and the landing gear lowered before lines and electrical are disconnected.
distractorExplanations.c: Unlocking before the landing gear is down risks the trailer dropping when the tractor moves.
distractorExplanations.d: Trailer brakes stay set (and chocks used) during uncoupling so the trailer cannot roll.

options.a: Be connected, with lights checked only at night
options.b: Be plugged in before air lines to power the brakes
options.c: Rest on the catwalk unsecured to avoid strain
options.d: Be connected and secure with working lights/ABS

distractorExplanations.a: Trailer lights and ABS power are required at all times, so the cord is checked on every coupling.
distractorExplanations.b: Trailer brakes are air-operated; the pigtail powers lights and ABS, not brake application.
distractorExplanations.c: An unsecured cord can snag, chafe or pull out; it should be connected and properly supported.

options.a: A small gap is fine if the locking lever is in the locked position
options.b: Jaws closed around the kingpin head, not the shank
options.c: Landing gear down and supporting the trailer weight
options.d: No gap between upper/lower fifth wheel; locked; lines secure

distractorExplanations.a: Any gap between upper and lower fifth wheel can mean a high hook; there must be no space.
distractorExplanations.b: The jaws must close around the kingpin shank; closing on the head is a failed coupling.
distractorExplanations.c: After coupling the landing gear is raised fully; the fifth wheel carries the trailer.

options.a: Drive slowly to a shop nearby
options.b: Set the trailer brakes and go
options.c: Raise fifth wheel height and go
options.d: Do not go—recouple/inspect lock

distractorExplanations.a: An unlocked trailer can separate at any speed; the coupling must be fixed before moving.
distractorExplanations.b: Trailer brakes do not secure the kingpin; a failed pull test means the jaws are not locked.
distractorExplanations.c: Changing height without recoupling and checking the lock leaves an unsafe coupling.

options.a: Rear of trailer swings opposite the turn
options.b: Trailer wheels track inside the tractor
options.c: Tractor drive wheels lose grip in a turn
options.d: Trailer rear swaying side to side at speed

distractorExplanations.b: That is off-tracking, where trailer wheels follow a shorter path than the tractor in a turn.
distractorExplanations.c: Losing drive-wheel traction is a skid or jackknife risk, not tail swing.
distractorExplanations.d: Side-to-side sway at speed is trailer sway or rearward amplification, not tail swing in a turn.

options.a: Brake firmly at the curve's apex
options.b: Slow before the curve; steady gently
options.c: Enter at the posted speed limit
options.d: Coast through in neutral to let it settle

distractorExplanations.a: Braking in the curve shifts weight and can cause rollover or skids; slow down before entering.
distractorExplanations.c: Posted curve speeds are set for cars; a loaded truck can roll over at or below the posted speed.
distractorExplanations.d: Coasting in neutral removes engine braking and control; keep in gear with steady speed.

options.a: Single units / sudden steering inputs at speed
options.b: Multiple units / gradual lane changes
options.c: Lower speeds with long single trailers
options.d: Multiple units / sudden steer inputs at speed

distractorExplanations.a: Rearward amplification grows with each added unit; a single trailer whips less than doubles or triples.
distractorExplanations.b: Gradual steering limits amplification; sudden steer inputs at speed are what crack the whip.
distractorExplanations.c: Amplification grows with speed and number of units, not with low-speed single-trailer driving.

options.a: Back toward the passenger side for a better view
options.b: Use mirrors only and back up at a steady speed
options.c: Turn the wheel the same way you want the trailer
options.d: Get out and look; use a helper when available

distractorExplanations.a: The CDL manual says back toward the driver's side, where you can see more directly.
distractorExplanations.b: Mirrors have blind spots; get out and look, and back slowly in the lowest reverse gear.
distractorExplanations.c: When backing a trailer you turn the steering wheel opposite the direction you want the trailer to go.

options.a: Drive wheels lock while trailer pushes
options.b: Trailer brakes apply slightly ahead
options.c: Speed is reduced before a curve
options.d: The trailer is fully loaded and sitting level

distractorExplanations.b: Trailer brakes leading the tractor tends to keep the rig straight; drive-wheel lockup causes jackknife.
distractorExplanations.c: Slowing before curves reduces risk; hard braking that locks drive wheels raises it.
distractorExplanations.d: Empty or lightly loaded trailers are more prone to skids and jackknife than loaded ones.

options.a: Same following distance as on dry pavement
options.b: More following distance and smoother inputs
options.c: Quick steering corrections to stop any sliding
options.d: Engine brake set to high for more control

distractorExplanations.a: Stopping distance grows on slippery surfaces, so following distance must increase.
distractorExplanations.c: Sudden steering on slick roads can start a skid or jackknife; inputs should be smooth.
distractorExplanations.d: The CDL manual says turn off the engine brake on slippery roads, as it can cause drive-wheel skids.

options.a: Swing wide to the left before starting the turn
options.b: Turn sharply and early so the trailer clears the curb
options.c: Start the turn sooner, as you would in a car
options.d: May need to go wider / set up earlier to avoid curb

distractorExplanations.a: Swinging left first invites drivers to pass on the right; turn wide as you complete the turn instead.
distractorExplanations.b: Off-tracking makes the trailer cut inside; turning early drags its wheels over the curb.
distractorExplanations.c: A long trailer off-tracks, so the turn starts later and wider than in a car.

options.a: Stops shorter than loaded since it is lighter
options.b: Is more stable, so harder braking is safe
options.c: Can be skid-prone on drive axle—adjust technique
options.d: Needs the trailer air supply knob pushed in

distractorExplanations.a: The CDL manual notes bobtail tractors can take longer to stop because there is less traction.
distractorExplanations.b: With little weight on the drive axle, hard braking can lock the drive wheels and skid.
distractorExplanations.d: When bobtailing the trailer supply (red) knob stays out so tractor air is not lost through open lines.

options.a: Can load the tractor and unload trailer axles
options.b: Moves weight rearward onto the trailer tandem axles
options.c: Shifts weight off the steer axle onto the drive axles
options.d: Does not occur when the fifth wheel is set forward

distractorExplanations.b: Braking shifts weight forward, not rearward onto the trailer axles.
distractorExplanations.c: Braking transfers weight forward onto the steer axle, not off it.
distractorExplanations.d: Weight transfer happens under any braking; fifth-wheel position only changes how it is shared.

cdl-combination-readiness-check-handling.explanation: Handling: Can load the tractor and unload trailer axles depending on setup. The exact effect depends on the setup.

options.a: Smooth brake/steer; proper speed; functioning trailer brakes
options.b: Using the trailer hand valve alone for stops on slick roads
options.c: Placing the heaviest part of the load at the rear of the trailer
options.d: Braking hard in curves so the trailer stays in line

distractorExplanations.b: Using the hand valve to stop can lock trailer wheels and start a trailer skid.
distractorExplanations.c: Poor load placement upsets balance; cargo should be spread with weight forward and low.
distractorExplanations.d: Hard braking in curves is a classic cause of trailer skids and jackknife.

options.a: Trailer swing to the outside at high speed
options.b: Jackknifing when drive wheels lock up
options.c: Striking curbs/vehicles on inside of turns
options.d: Rollover from a high center of gravity

distractorExplanations.a: Outside swing at speed is rearward amplification; off-tracking is the trailer cutting inside a turn.
distractorExplanations.b: Jackknife comes from drive-wheel lockup under braking, not from turn path.
distractorExplanations.d: Rollover depends on center of gravity and speed; off-tracking concerns the inside path of the trailer.

options.a: Trailer swing/rollover risk
options.b: Fifth-wheel jaws unlocking
options.c: Tractor protection valve trip
options.d: Drive-axle brake fade

distractorExplanations.b: A properly locked fifth wheel does not unlock from steering; the danger is trailer swing and rollover.
distractorExplanations.c: The TP valve responds to trailer air loss, not steering maneuvers.
distractorExplanations.d: Fade comes from heat during long braking, not from a quick lane change.

options.a: Light, steady brake pressure all the way down the hill
options.b: Downshifting partway down once the speed picks up
options.c: Highest gear with the trailer hand valve for braking
options.d: Proper gear and controlled braking plan before the hill

distractorExplanations.a: Constant light braking overheats the brakes and causes fade; use the right gear and snub braking.
distractorExplanations.b: Downshifting after speed builds may be impossible; select the low gear before the downgrade.
distractorExplanations.c: A high gear gives little engine braking, and the hand valve should not be used to slow the rig.

options.a: Tractor items only, since the trailer has its own inspection
options.b: Lights and tires, with coupling checked at the first stop
options.c: Fifth wheel, lines, lights, tires, brakes, coupling integrity
options.d: Fifth wheel and kingpin, with air lines checked weekly

distractorExplanations.a: The driver's pre-trip covers the whole combination, including trailer and coupling.
distractorExplanations.b: The coupling is checked before driving; a faulty coupling can separate on the first turn.
distractorExplanations.d: Air lines are inspected on every pre-trip; leaks or crossed lines affect trailer brakes.

options.a: Correct paint color coding
options.b: Lubrication with engine grease
options.c: Matching part numbers on both
options.d: Cracks, missing seals, leaks

distractorExplanations.a: Color coding helps match lines, but the seal check looks for cracks, missing seals and leaks.
distractorExplanations.b: Gladhand seals are not greased; the check is for cracked or missing seals and air leaks.
distractorExplanations.c: Part numbers do not show seal condition; inspect for cracks, missing seals and leaks.

options.a: Whether it is fully lowered when driving
options.b: Crank handle stowed loosely for quick use
options.c: Paint and rust on the outer legs only
options.d: Cracks, missing pins, poor engagement

distractorExplanations.a: Landing gear must be fully raised when driving; the inspection looks for damage and engagement.
distractorExplanations.b: The crank handle must be secured; a loose handle can swing and cause injury or damage.
distractorExplanations.c: Cosmetic rust is not the concern; look for cracks, missing pins and poor engagement.

options.a: Tail, stop, turn, clearance, plate as required
options.b: Stop and turn lights, with clearance lamps optional
options.c: Tail and clearance lights, checked only at night
options.d: Turn signals and the trailer ABS lamp alone

distractorExplanations.b: Clearance and marker lamps are required on trailers; they are not optional.
distractorExplanations.c: Lights are checked on every pre-trip, and stop and turn signals are required at all times.
distractorExplanations.d: Turn signals alone are not enough; tail, stop, clearance and plate lights must also work.

options.a: Expected where lines cross the frame
options.b: A leak/failure risk—secure/repair
options.c: Fine if wrapped with duct tape
options.d: A problem only when it leaks air

distractorExplanations.a: Chafing is never expected; lines must be supported so they do not rub through.
distractorExplanations.c: Tape hides damage and does not restore the line; chafed lines are secured or replaced.
distractorExplanations.d: Chafed lines can fail suddenly; they are repaired before they start leaking.

options.a: Check only that it is greased evenly
options.b: Measure the kingpin for fifth-wheel height
options.c: Look for cracks, bends, improper locking
options.d: Check it once a year at annual inspection

distractorExplanations.a: Grease does not reveal cracks or bends; inspect the kingpin itself for damage and locking.
distractorExplanations.b: Fifth-wheel height is set separately; kingpin inspection looks for cracks, bends and locking.
distractorExplanations.d: The kingpin and coupling are checked on every pre-trip, not only at the annual inspection.

options.a: Tread of 4/32 inch minimum on trailer tires
options.b: Matching brands and duals touching
options.c: Valve stems and hub caps only
options.d: Inflation, tread, cuts, dual mating

distractorExplanations.a: The 4/32-inch minimum applies to steer tires; other tires, including trailer tires, need 2/32 inch.
distractorExplanations.b: Duals must not touch each other; brand matching is not an inspection requirement.
distractorExplanations.c: Valve stems are part of it, but inflation, tread, cuts and dual spacing must be checked.

options.a: Latches, seals, straps/chains per cargo type
options.b: Door latches only, since cargo is the shipper's job
options.c: Straps checked once at loading, not en route
options.d: Seals and tarps, with tiedowns checked weekly

distractorExplanations.b: FMCSA rules make the driver responsible for checking cargo securement, not only the shipper.
distractorExplanations.c: Securement is rechecked within the first 50 miles and periodically during the trip.
distractorExplanations.d: Tiedowns are checked before every trip and en route, not on a weekly schedule.

options.a: Are normal as long as the trailer still rides level
options.b: Matter only when the trailer is running empty
options.c: Can cause lean/poor brake geometry—OOS risk
options.d: Are fixed by raising tire pressure

distractorExplanations.a: Any air bag leak is a defect; a trailer can look level while losing support pressure.
distractorExplanations.b: Leaking air bags affect ride height and brake geometry loaded or empty.
distractorExplanations.d: Tire pressure does not compensate for suspension air loss; the leak must be repaired.

options.a: Is checked only on the tractor axles
options.b: Must be within limits like tractor
options.c: Can exceed limits with auto slacks
options.d: Is not checked on spring brake axles

distractorExplanations.a: Trailer axle brakes have the same stroke limits and are part of the inspection.
distractorExplanations.c: Automatic slack adjusters do not excuse overstroke; out-of-limit stroke is a defect.
distractorExplanations.d: Spring brake chambers still have service pushrod stroke limits that must be met.

options.a: Stay lit while the trailer moves
options.b: Light only when air pressure is low
options.c: Behave per design—note faults
options.d: Stay off during the start-up check

distractorExplanations.a: A lamp that stays lit while moving signals an ABS fault, not normal operation.
distractorExplanations.b: The trailer ABS lamp reports ABS faults, not air pressure; it has nothing to do with low air.
distractorExplanations.d: The lamp should come on briefly as a bulb check; staying dark can mean a failed bulb or system.

options.a: Not fully coupled / unsafe
options.b: Normal fifth-wheel tilt
options.c: Proper coupling height
options.d: Need for more fifth-wheel grease

distractorExplanations.b: A visible gap is not normal tilt; it can mean a high hook with the kingpin not in the jaws.
distractorExplanations.c: A gap shows the trailer is not seated on the fifth wheel; it is not a sign of correct height.
distractorExplanations.d: Grease does not close a gap; the trailer must be recoupled and checked.

options.a: Stowed in the cab
options.b: Present and secured
options.c: Attached when loaded
options.d: Left slack to drag

distractorExplanations.a: Safety chains must be attached between the units where required, not stored in the cab.
distractorExplanations.c: Safety devices are required whenever towing, loaded or empty.
distractorExplanations.d: Chains must have only enough slack for turns; dragging chains wear and can fail.

options.a: Lines and locks, with landing gear left partly down for support
options.b: Electrical and locks, with air lines rechecked at the first fuel stop
options.c: Lines, electrical, locks, landing gear up, chocks removed appropriately
options.d: Landing gear up and chocks removed, with the jaws checked by the yard

distractorExplanations.a: Landing gear must be fully raised before driving; partly down gear can catch on rail crossings.
distractorExplanations.b: Air lines are checked before moving; crossed or loose lines affect trailer brakes immediately.
distractorExplanations.d: The driver personally verifies the jaws are locked; it cannot be left to yard staff.

options.a: Optional on rear trailers
options.b: A violation/inspection item
options.c: Allowed if under 26,000 lb
options.d: A defect only for hazmat

distractorExplanations.a: Where splash guards are required, they are required on every applicable unit, not optional.
distractorExplanations.c: Weight does not exempt a vehicle where mud flaps are required; missing ones are a violation.
distractorExplanations.d: Mud flap requirements apply to all vehicles covered by the rule, not just hazmat loads.

options.a: Proper speed, smooth control, functioning brakes/ABS technique
options.b: Hard braking in curves to keep the trailer behind the tractor
options.c: Running empty trailers, which are less likely to jackknife
options.d: Using the trailer hand valve to stop on slippery roads

distractorExplanations.b: Hard braking in curves is a leading cause of jackknife; brake before the curve.
distractorExplanations.c: Empty trailers are more prone to jackknife because their wheels lock more easily.
distractorExplanations.d: Using the hand valve can lock trailer wheels and start a trailer jackknife.

options.a: Cargo is loaded low and spread evenly
options.b: Speed is cut before entering curves
options.c: Tires are all inflated to the correct pressure
options.d: CG is high and speed in curves is excessive

distractorExplanations.a: Low, evenly spread cargo raises the rollover threshold; a high center of gravity lowers it.
distractorExplanations.b: Slowing before curves reduces rollover risk; excessive curve speed increases it.
distractorExplanations.c: Correct inflation helps stability; rollover risk comes from high CG and curve speed.

options.a: Ease off throttle/brake appropriately; steer gently to recover
options.b: Brake hard to lock the tractor wheels and stop the swing quickly
options.c: Accelerate firmly to pull the trailer back in line behind you
options.d: Steer sharply toward the swing and hold it until it stops

distractorExplanations.b: Locking the tractor wheels can cause a tractor jackknife; release the brakes to regain traction.
distractorExplanations.c: Hard acceleration can break drive-wheel traction and worsen the swing; ease off smoothly.
distractorExplanations.d: Sharp, held steering can overcorrect and roll the trailer; steering inputs should be gentle.

cdl-combination-readiness-check-safety-0.explanation: Safety: Ease off throttle/brake appropriately; steer gently to recover if trained. Use recovery steering only as trained.

options.a: The same gaps as passenger cars
options.b: Smaller gaps due to air brakes
options.c: Larger gaps than passenger cars
options.d: A two-second following gap

distractorExplanations.a: Combinations are longer and heavier and need more stopping distance than cars.
distractorExplanations.b: Air brakes add lag time, so combinations need larger following gaps, not smaller ones.
distractorExplanations.d: The CDL rule is one second per 10 feet of length (plus one over 40 mph), far more than two seconds.

options.a: Light steady braking all the way down
options.b: Downshift once speed builds on the hill
options.c: Use the same gear used going uphill
options.d: Plan gear early; control heat in brakes

distractorExplanations.a: Continuous light braking builds heat and causes fade; select the gear early and snub brake.
distractorExplanations.b: Downshifting after speed builds may be impossible; choose the low gear before the grade.
distractorExplanations.c: The CDL manual says the proper downhill gear is usually lower than the gear used to climb.

options.a: Only a cargo damage claim later
options.b: Handling/rollover/brake issues
options.c: Improved traction in tight curves
options.d: Air leaks at the gladhands

distractorExplanations.a: Shifting cargo changes the center of gravity and can cause loss of control, not just damage claims.
distractorExplanations.c: Shifting weight upsets balance in curves and raises rollover risk, not traction.
distractorExplanations.d: Gladhand leaks come from seals and coupling; cargo shifts affect handling and braking.

options.a: Only when the trailer is fully loaded
options.b: Off course, so speed up to stay more stable
options.c: Into other lanes—reduce speed, both hands
options.d: Mainly at low speed, so drive faster

distractorExplanations.a: Empty or light trailers are the most affected by wind because they weigh less.
distractorExplanations.b: Higher speed makes wind gusts more dangerous; slow down and keep both hands on the wheel.
distractorExplanations.d: Wind effects worsen with speed; slowing down is the correct response.

options.a: Allows closer following using taillights
options.b: Calls for high beams near other traffic
options.c: Reduces off-tracking as traffic is lighter
options.d: Increases judgment error risk—slow and scan

distractorExplanations.a: Reduced visibility at night calls for more following distance, not less.
distractorExplanations.b: High beams are dimmed for oncoming and followed vehicles to avoid blinding drivers.
distractorExplanations.c: Off-tracking depends on trailer length and turn radius, not traffic or time of day.

options.a: Hold light, steady pressure on brakes
options.b: Pump the brakes rapidly to cool them
options.c: Use proper gear/retarders/snub method
options.d: Use the trailer hand valve to brake

distractorExplanations.a: Steady light braking keeps heating the brakes and causes fade on long hills.
distractorExplanations.b: Pumping wastes air and does not cool brakes; use proper gear and snub braking.
distractorExplanations.d: The hand valve is not used for slowing on grades; it overheats trailer brakes and risks skids.

options.a: Easier than braking, so steer first and brake during the turn
options.b: Harder with trailer, so steer sharply, then brake hard in the turn
options.c: Harder with trailer—brake first if possible, then steer smoothly
options.d: Safe at any speed if the trailer has working ABS

distractorExplanations.a: Braking while turning can lock wheels and cause a skid or jackknife; brake before steering.
distractorExplanations.b: Sharp steering with hard braking in the turn invites rollover or jackknife.
distractorExplanations.d: ABS helps prevent lockup but cannot prevent rollover from sudden maneuvers at speed.

options.a: Keep speed and brake on the deck
options.b: Brake firmly once on the span
options.c: Use cruise control for steadiness
options.d: Slow early; avoid sudden inputs

distractorExplanations.a: Bridges freeze first; braking on an icy deck can cause a skid. Slow before reaching it.
distractorExplanations.b: Firm braking on a slippery deck risks lockup; slow down early, before the bridge.
distractorExplanations.c: The CDL manual says do not use cruise control on slippery roads.

options.a: Get out and look / use a spotter
options.b: Back slowly using the mirrors
options.c: Sound the horn and keep backing
options.d: Rely on the backup alarm alone

distractorExplanations.b: Mirrors leave blind spots behind the trailer; get out and look or use a spotter.
distractorExplanations.c: The horn warns others but does not show you what is behind; check before backing.
distractorExplanations.d: A backup alarm warns people but does not let you see obstacles behind the trailer.

options.a: Brake fade from overheated drums on long downgrades
options.b: Air line separation at the gladhand couplers
options.c: Shock loads that can upset combination stability
options.d: Tractor protection valve trips on downgrades

distractorExplanations.a: Fade is a braking heat problem; smooth shifting prevents drivetrain shock loads.
distractorExplanations.b: Air line separation is a coupling issue, not something proper shifting prevents.
distractorExplanations.d: The TP valve responds to trailer air loss, not to gear changes.

options.a: Check for smell/smoke/pull; inspect when safe
options.b: Drain the tanks and rebuild the air before going
options.c: Cool the brakes with water at the next stop
options.d: Push the trailer knob in to reset the brakes

distractorExplanations.b: Draining tanks does not reveal brake damage; check for smell, smoke and pulling, then inspect.
distractorExplanations.c: Water on hot drums can crack them; let brakes cool naturally and inspect when safe.
distractorExplanations.d: A hard stop does not require resetting the supply knob; check the brakes for heat damage.
